description: Add a claude auth-preflight to the container ensure path so a container-mode sidecar fails closed (writes a durable stall marker, dispatches no worker) when claude is unauthenticated inside cam-worker.

userStories.title: Register container-auth-unavailable stall reason
userStories.description: As the sidecar-stalled marker reader, I need the new 'container-auth-unavailable' reason registered so the auth-preflight marker round-trips instead of being rejected as an unrecognized discriminator.
acceptanceCriteria: 'container-auth-unavailable' is added to the SidecarStalledReason type, the VALID_REASONS array, AND the JSDoc reason list in src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts, so readSidecarStalledMarker round-trips a marker carrying that reason. [oracle: grep -q "container-auth-unavailable" src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts]
readSidecarStalledMarker accepts a written marker with reason 'container-auth-unavailable' and returns it (does not return null). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Load-bearing per issue gotcha: ALL THREE sites in src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts must gain the reason -- the SidecarStalledReason type (~:33), the VALID_REASONS readonly array (~:47), and the JSDoc list (~:26-33). If VALID_REASONS is missed, readSidecarStalledMarker silently returns null (:70-72). This is the 'JSON reader shape guards: validate discriminator fields' pattern (scripts/cam/patterns.md, US-R2-001): the discriminator must be in VALID_REASONS to pass the guard. Test template: test/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.test.ts (round-trip write+read at real tmpdir). No external library, no fetch.

userStories.title: Add in-container claude auth probe module
userStories.description: As the container ensure path, I need a pure in-container claude auth probe (mirroring container-firewall.ts) so I can detect an unauthenticated cam-worker before any worker is dispatched.
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/supervisor/container-auth.ts exports buildAuthCheckExecArgv(containerName) returning the non-interactive argv ['exec', containerName, 'claude', 'auth', 'status', '--json'] (no -it, no sudo). [oracle: grep -q "'exec', containerName, 'claude', 'auth', 'status', '--json'" src/supervisor/container-auth.ts]

applyContainerAuthCheck(containerName, spawnFn) runs the argv via spawnFn('docker', argv), parses the claude auth JSON loggedIn field reusing the parse logic convention from src/commands/run-auth-preflight.ts, and returns a discriminated {ok} result; it NEVER throws (mirrors applyContainerFirewall). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/container-auth.test.ts]

class ContainerAuthError extends Error carries a stderrTail/message and sets name='ContainerAuthError', mirroring FirewallError. [oracle: grep -q "class ContainerAuthError" src/supervisor/container-auth.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New file src/supervisor/container-auth.ts + test/supervisor/container-auth.test.ts. Mirror src/supervisor/container-firewall.ts structure exactly: pure applyContainer* helper returns a discriminated {ok:true} | {ok:false,exitCode,stderrTail} union and NEVER throws; the typed ContainerAuthError is thrown by the caller (US-003), not here. The probe is non-interactive: argv has NO -it and NO sudo (unlike buildFirewallExecArgv which uses sudo). Reuse the parseAuthJson/loggedIn convention from src/commands/run-auth-preflight.ts:44-56,125 (loggedIn !== true => not ok). Do NOT reuse dockerExecWrap (src/commands/docker-exec.ts:34) -- it builds an interactive '-it' STRING for tmux panes, wrong for a spawnSync probe. Test DI fake template: test/commands/run-auth-preflight.test.ts (makeFakeAuthSpawn + loggedInPayload) for the auth JSON; container-firewall's test for the docker spawnFn shape. No external library, no fetch.

userStories.title: Wire auth-check step into ensureWorkerContainer
userStories.description: As ensureWorkerContainer, I need an applyAuthCheckIfPresent step (mirroring applyFirewallIfPresent) that runs the probe and throws ContainerAuthError when the container is unauthenticated, so a reused running container that lost its OAuth token is still caught before dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: ensureWorkerContainer (src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts) gains applyAuthCheckIfPresent(containerName, authCheckSpawnFn): a complete no-op when authCheckSpawnFn is undefined (host mode), otherwise it runs applyContainerAuthCheck and throws ContainerAuthError on loggedIn!==true. [oracle: grep -q "applyAuthCheckIfPresent" src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts]

applyAuthCheckIfPresent is called unconditionally AFTER applyConfigIfPresent and BEFORE the final return, so a reused running container (no docker reconcile call) that lost its token is still caught. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts]

The authCheckSpawnFn seam is added to EnsureWorkerContainerOptions and wired from spawnSync in makeProductionEnsureContainerFn, mirroring the firewall closure. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts]
Host mode (authCheckSpawnFn undefined) remains a complete no-op and all existing ensure-container tests stay green. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Edit src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts + test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts. Follow the apply*-DI-seam pattern exactly: applyFirewallIfPresent (:198-207) is the template. Slot the call AFTER applyConfigIfPresent (~:417) and BEFORE the final return (~:419) -- auth depends on the config step having repaired /home/bun/.claude ownership first, and it must be unconditional to catch the running->reuse branch. Add authCheckSpawnFn to EnsureWorkerContainerOptions and wire the production closure from spawnSync in makeProductionEnsureContainerFn (~:439-508, mirror the firewall closure ~:463-491) and pass it into the ensureWorkerContainer call (~:497-506). Depends on US-002 (imports applyContainerAuthCheck + ContainerAuthError). Test DI template: test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts makeRecordingSpawnFn returning a non-zero/loggedIn:false docker exec to simulate a failing probe (no real container). No external library, no fetch.

userStories.title: Catch ContainerAuthError in the ensure-guard and fail closed
userStories.description: As runContainerEnsureGuard, I need to catch ContainerAuthError and mirror the FirewallError fail-closed path (write the durable stall marker, abort boot) so no worker is dispatched into an unauthenticated container.
acceptanceCriteria: runContainerEnsureGuard (src/commands/sidecar.ts) catches ContainerAuthError and mirrors the FirewallError path exactly: it writes .claude/.cam-sidecar-stalled.json via writeSidecarStalledMarker with reason 'container-auth-unavailable' and detail from the error, then returns true so boot aborts before the loop. [oracle: grep -q "container-auth-unavailable" src/commands/sidecar.ts]

The auth branch copies the FirewallError branch (writes a marker), NOT the ContainerConfigError/ToolchainMismatchError branches (which deliberately write no marker). [oracle: bun test test/commands/sidecar-auth.test.ts]

When the injected ensureContainerFn throws ContainerAuthError, the sidecar loop is never entered (runSidecarLoopFn spy proves it) and readSidecarStalledMarker returns reason 'container-auth-unavailable' with the error detail. [oracle: bun test test/commands/sidecar-auth.test.ts]
Host mode and the claude backend path are unchanged; the full quality spine is green. [oracle: bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Edit src/commands/sidecar.ts (runContainerEnsureGuard ~:3331-3370) + new test/commands/sidecar-auth.test.ts. CRITICAL gotcha: mirror the FirewallError branch (:3344-3354, which WRITES the marker), NOT ContainerConfigError (:3355-3360) or ToolchainMismatchError (:3361-3367), which do NOT write a marker -- CAM-396 requires a durable marker. Add the `if (e instanceof ContainerAuthError)` branch importing ContainerAuthError from US-002 and writeSidecarStalledMarker/SIDECAR_STALLED_FILENAME already imported. Depends on US-001 (reason registered so the marker round-trips), US-002 (ContainerAuthError type), US-003 (ensure path actually throws it). Test template: test/commands/sidecar-firewall.test.ts -- runSidecar with an ensureContainerFn that throws + a runSidecarLoopFn spy proving the loop never runs, plus readSidecarStalledMarker asserting reason/detail/writtenAt. No production code reads the marker today (ADR-0026 boot surface not wired), but the round-trip + fail-closed abort are the behavioral contract. No external library, no fetch.
